321	def recommend_scheme(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size") -> Params:
322	    """Return the :class:`Params` of the scheme best fitting capacity/budgets.
323	
324	    The cross-scheme counterpart of :func:`recommend`: instead of choosing
325	    only among Merkle configurations, enumerate every configuration
326	    :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS
327	    with ``w`` 4 and 8) and every Merkle configuration with ``w`` in
328	    ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — keep those whose ``capacity``
329	    covers the requested signature count and that satisfy both budgets, and
330	    rank the feasible set. The one-time candidates cover one signature and
331	    are present only when ``capacity == 1``; a request for more than one
332	    signature leaves the Merkle configurations as the only candidates.
333	
334	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
335	    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
336	    signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and on the
337	    verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`). Each entry is
338	    either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at
339	    least one entry must be set.
340	
341	    ``prefer="size"`` (the default) ranks candidates by ``sig_bytes`` first
342	    and ``steps`` second; ``prefer="speed"`` reverses the two. Both share
343	    the same ascending tie-break afterwards: spare capacity
344	    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), the scheme
345	    name lexicographically, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing
346	    parameter sorted ahead of any value. The first candidate after sorting
347	    is returned as a :class:`Params`.
348	
349	    Validation runs capacity first, budgets second and ``prefer`` last. A
350	    non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a boolean, non-integer or
351	    out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal
352	    ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``), an unknown
353	    ``prefer`` value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises
354	    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
355	    no keys and changes no state.
356	    """
357	    if (
358	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
359	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
360	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
361	    ):
362	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
363	    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
364	        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 2-tuple of budget limits")
365	    if len(budgets) != 2:
366	        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly two entries")
367	
368	    labels = ("signature", "steps")
369	    limits = []
370	    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
371	        if budget is None:
372	            limits.append(None)
373	        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
374	            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
375	        else:
376	            limits.append(budget)
377	    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
378	        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
379	    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
380	        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
381	    signature_limit, steps_limit = limits
382	
383	    candidates: list[Params] = []
384	    if capacity == 1:
385	        candidates.append(profile("lamport"))
386	        for w in (4, 8):
387	            candidates.append(profile("wots", w=w))
388	    for w in (4, 8):
389	        for height in range(1, 9):
390	            candidate = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)
391	            if candidate.capacity >= capacity:
392	                candidates.append(candidate)
393	
394	    feasible = []
395	    for candidate in candidates:
396	        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
397	            continue
398	        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
399	            continue
400	        feasible.append(candidate)
401	    if not feasible:
402	        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")
403	
404	    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
405	        tail = (
406	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
407	            candidate.scheme,
408	            candidate.w is not None,
409	            candidate.w,
410	            candidate.height is not None,
411	            candidate.height,
412	        )
413	        if prefer == "speed":
414	            return (candidate.steps, candidate.sig_bytes) + tail
415	        return (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) + tail
416	
417	    return min(feasible, key=ranking)
418

423	    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.
424	
425	    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
426	    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
427	    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
428	    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.
429	
430	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
431	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
432	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
433	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
434	    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)
435	    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
436	    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
437	    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.
438	
439	    ``prefer="size"`` ranks candidates lexicographically by signature wire
440	    length, proof wire length, checkpoint bytes, steps, leaf count, ``w`` and
441	    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
442	    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
443	    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.
444	
445	    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
446	    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
447	    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
448	    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
449	    no state.
450	    """
451	    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
452	        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
453	    if len(budgets) != 4:
454	        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
455	    if (
456	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
457	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
458	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
459	    ):
460	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
461	    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
462	        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
463	
464	    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
465	    limits = []
466	    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
467	        if budget is None:
468	            limits.append(None)
469	        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
470	            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
471	        else:
472	            limits.append(budget)
473	    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
474	        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
475	    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits
476	
477	    feasible = []
478	    for w in (4, 8):
479	        for height in range(1, 9):
480	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
481	            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
482	                continue
483	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
484	                continue
485	            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
486	                continue
487	            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
488	                continue
489	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
490	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
491	                continue
492	            feasible.append((storage, steps))
493	    if not feasible:
494	        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")
495	
496	    def ranking(candidate: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
497	        storage, steps = candidate
498	        ordered = (
499	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
500	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
501	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
502	            steps,
503	            storage.leaf_count,
504	            storage.w,
505	            storage.height,
506	        )
507	        if prefer == "speed":
508	            return (steps,) + ordered
509	        return ordered
510	
511	    feasible.sort(key=ranking)
512	    return feasible[0][0]

555	def merkle_deployment_frontier(
556	    capacity: Any, budgets: Any
557	) -> tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, ...]:
558	    """Return every feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployment as a tuple.
559	
560	    Where :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment` ranks the feasible configs and
561	    returns one, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
562	    inspect the trade-off between storage, signature, proof and verification
563	    costs: it enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times
564	    ``height`` from 1 to 8 — whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity``, keeps
565	    those satisfying every set budget, reusing
566	    :func:`merkle_storage_profile` for the wire sizes and
567	    :func:`profile` for the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count, and
568	    drops every dominated candidate.
569	
570	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
571	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
572	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
573	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
574	    standalone proof wire length
575	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and on the per-signature
576	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s ``steps``).
577	    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
578	    integer, and at least one entry must be set; every bound is inclusive.
579	
580	    A feasible profile *A* dominates another feasible profile *B* when
581	    ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on all four metrics — checkpoint bytes,
582	    signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes and verifier steps — and strictly
583	    smaller on at least one; every dominated candidate is dropped and the
584	    survivors are deduplicated by value. No preference is applied, so a
585	    configuration trading speed for size (or the reverse) is never discarded
586	    ahead of the dominance test. The returned tuple is sorted stably and
587	    ascending by verifier steps, signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes,
588	    checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height``.
589	
590	    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length or otherwise
591	    illegal ``budgets`` tuple, an out-of-range ``capacity`` or the absence of
592	    any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
593	    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
594	    """
595	    limits = _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets)
596	    if (
597	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
598	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
599	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
600	    ):
601	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
602	    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits
603	
604	    candidates: list[tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]] = []
605	    for w in (4, 8):
606	        for height in range(1, 9):
607	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
608	            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
609	                continue
610	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
611	                continue
612	            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
613	                continue
614	            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
615	                continue
616	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
617	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
618	                continue
619	            candidates.append((storage, steps))
620	    if not candidates:
621	        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")
622	
623	    def dominates(
624	        a: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
625	        b: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
626	    ) -> bool:
627	        a_storage, a_steps = a
628	        b_storage, b_steps = b
629	        no_worse = (
630	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes <= b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
631	            and a_storage.signature_wire_bytes <= b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
632	            and a_storage.proof_wire_bytes <= b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
633	            and a_steps <= b_steps
634	        )
635	        strictly_better = (
636	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes < b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
637	            or a_storage.signature_wire_bytes < b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
638	            or a_storage.proof_wire_bytes < b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
639	            or a_steps < b_steps
640	        )
641	        return no_worse and strictly_better
642	
643	    non_dominated = [
644	        candidate
645	        for candidate in candidates
646	        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in candidates)
647	    ]
648

688	def recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted(
689	    capacity: Any,
690	    budgets: Any,
691	    weights: Any,
692	) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
693	    """Pick one non-dominated Merkle deployment by weighted normalised costs.
694	
695	    Computes :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier` exactly once and ranks the
696	    returned feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployments by a
697	    caller-supplied linear score over four costs: the checkpoint bytes
698	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), one signature wire
699	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), one
700	    standalone proof wire length
701	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and the per-signature
702	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
703	    ``steps``).
704	
705	    ``weights`` must be a four-tuple in that same order — checkpoint bytes,
706	    signature wire bytes, standalone proof wire bytes and per-signature
707	    chain steps. Every weight must be a non-boolean, non-negative integer
708	    and at least one must be positive. Each of the four costs is min-max
709	    normalised over the whole frontier as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with
710	    a zero span scoring ``0``; the weighted score is the sum of the four
711	    normalised costs times their weights, divided by the weight total, all
712	    compared as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating
713	    point anywhere. The survivor with the smallest score is returned; equal
714	    scores are broken ascending by checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and
715	    ``height``. The candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
716	    duplicated: the frontier is the only source of candidates and is called
717	    exactly once.
718	
719	    ``capacity`` and the four-tuple ``budgets`` follow
720	    :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget,
721	    exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation
722	    raises exactly as that function does (and is screened before
723	    ``weights``). A non-tuple ``weights`` or a non-integer member raises
724	    ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a boolean, negative or all-zero
725	    weight raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no
726	    randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
727	    """
728	    frontier = merkle_deployment_frontier(capacity, budgets)
729	    validated_weights = _validate_deployment_weights(weights)
730	
731	    def metrics(storage: MerkleStorageProfile) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
732	        return (
733	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
734	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
735	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
736	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
737	        )
738	
739	    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(storage) for storage in frontier)
740	    spans = tuple(
741	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
742	        for i in range(4)
743	    )
744	    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)
745	
746	    def ranking(
747	        storage: MerkleStorageProfile,
748	    ) -> tuple[Fraction, int, int, int, int]:
749	        score = Fraction(0)
750	        for value, weight, (low, high) in zip(metrics(storage), validated_weights, spans):
751	            if high > low:
752	                score += weight * Fraction(value - low, high - low)
753	        score /= weight_total
754	        return (
755	            score,
756	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
757	            storage.leaf_count,
758	            storage.w,
759	            storage.height,
760	        )
761	
762	    return min(frontier, key=ranking)

812	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s

823	    source of candidates — the candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering

830	    subtracted from every candidate's score to give that scenario's

832	    scenarios (the minimax-regret choice), then by the sum of the
833	    regrets, then by the tuple of per-scenario scores, all ascending. A
834	    complete tie is broken ascending by checkpoint bytes, leaf count,
835	    ``w`` and ``height``, and the first survivor is returned as a
836	    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.

839	    :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget,
840	    exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation

842	    ``scenarios``). A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or a
843	    non-integer weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
844	    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight
845	    raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness,
846	    generates no keys and changes no state.
847	    """

849	    validated_scenarios = _validate_deployment_weight_scenarios(scenarios)
850	
851	    def metrics(storage: MerkleStorageProfile) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
852	        return (
853	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
854	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
855	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
856	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
857	        )
858	
859	    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(storage) for storage in frontier)
860	    spans = tuple(
861	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
862	        for i in range(4)
863	    )
864	
865	    def normalised(row: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
866	        return tuple(
867	            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
868	            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)

870	
871	    normalised_rows = tuple(normalised(row) for row in metric_rows)

877	                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, row)),

881	            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
882	        )
883	
884	    score_rows = tuple(scenario_scores(row) for row in normalised_rows)
885	    scenario_best = tuple(
886	        min(row[scenario_index] for row in score_rows)
887	        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
888	    )
889	
890	    def ranking(
891	        entry: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, tuple[Fraction, ...]],
892	    ) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, tuple[Fraction, ...], int, int, int, int]:

894	        regrets = tuple(
895	            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)

897	        return (
898	            max(regrets),
899	            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),

901	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,

1166	    - ``k`` is the number of selected leaf indices;
1167	    - ``wots`` is the upper bound on W-OTS hash-chain steps for all ``k``
1168	      signatures: ``k * 67 * 15`` for ``w=4`` or ``k * 34 * 255`` for
1169	      ``w=8``;

1171	      key: ``k`` (authentication-path deduplication never reduces it);
1172	    - ``batch`` is the internal-node hash count when each signature carries a
1173	      full authentication path: ``k * height``, every path repeated in full;
1174	    - ``multi`` is the internal-node hash count of the deduplicated
1175	      multi-proof merge: ``sum(len({i >> l for i in indices}) for l in
1176	      range(1, height + 1))`` — at each level every distinct parent node is
1177	      hashed exactly once.
1178	
1179	    Instances are frozen, support positional construction and compare (and
1180	    hash) by value; no key material or randomness is involved.
1181	    """

1184	    height: int
1185	    k: int
1186	    wots: int
1187	    leaf: int
1188	    batch: int
1189	    multi: int

1192	def merkle_verify_profile(w: Any, height: Any, indices: Any) -> MerkleVerifyProfile:
1193	    """Return the frozen :class:`MerkleVerifyProfile` verification-hash counts.
1194	
1195	    Counts the SHA-256 work a verifier spends on a batch proof versus a
1196	    multi-proof over the same leaf set ``indices``. ``w`` must be 4 or 8 and
1197	    ``height`` a non-boolean integer from 1 to 8; ``indices`` must be a
1198	    non-empty tuple of strictly increasing, non-boolean integers, each in
1199	    ``0 .. 2 ** height - 1``. A non-tuple ``indices`` or a member that is not
1200	    an ``int`` raises ``TypeError``; an empty set, a boolean member, an
1201	    out-of-range, duplicate or out-of-order index, or an illegal ``w`` /
1202	    ``height`` raises ``ValueError``.
1203	
1204	    With ``k = len(indices)``, the fields are: ``wots`` the W-OTS chain-step
1205	    upper bound (``k * 67 * 15`` for ``w=4``, ``k * 34 * 255`` for ``w=8``);
1206	    ``leaf = k`` (one leaf hash per selected leaf, never reduced by path
1207	    deduplication); ``batch = k * height`` (each signature repeats its full
1208	    authentication path); and ``multi`` the deduplicated internal-node count,
1209	    ``sum(len({i >> l for i in indices}) for l in range(1, height + 1))`` —
1210	    at each level each distinct parent is hashed once. The estimate is pure:
1211	    no keys are generated, no randomness is drawn and no state is changed.
1212	    """
1213	    w = _validate_w(w)
1214	    height = _validate_height(height)
1215	    if not isinstance(indices, tuple):
1216	        raise TypeError("indices must be a tuple of leaf indices")
1217	    if not indices:
1218	        raise ValueError("indices must not be empty")
1219	    if any(isinstance(index, bool) for index in indices):
1220	        raise ValueError("index members must not be booleans")
1221	    if any(not isinstance(index, int) for index in indices):
1222	        raise TypeError("every index must be an integer")
1223	    leaf_count = 1 << height
1224	    if any(index < 0 or index >= leaf_count for index in indices):
1225	        raise ValueError("every index must be within the tree's leaf range")
1226	    if any(former >= latter for former, latter in zip(indices, indices[1:])):
1227	        raise ValueError("indices must be strictly increasing and unique")
1228	
1229	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
1230	    k = len(indices)
1231	    wots = k * (l1 + l2) * (b - 1)
1232	    leaf = k
1233	    batch = k * height
1234	    multi = sum(
1235	        len({index >> level for index in indices})
1236	        for level in range(1, height + 1)
1237	    )
1238	    return MerkleVerifyProfile(
1239	        w=w, height=height, k=k, wots=wots, leaf=leaf, batch=batch, multi=multi
1240	    )

1252	    - ``costs`` is one five-tuple per input group, in group order; each entry
1253	      is ``(mode, wots, leaf, internal, total)`` where ``mode`` is the chosen
1254	      transport name, ``wots`` is the group's W-OTS hash-chain-step upper
1255	      bound, ``leaf`` its leaf-hash count, ``internal`` its internal-node hash
1256	      count (``batch`` of :class:`MerkleVerifyProfile` for a ``"batch"``
1257	      group, ``multi`` for a ``"multiproof"`` group) and ``total`` the sum of
1258	      those three hash counts for the group — repeated groups are billed
1259	      separately;
1260	    - ``total`` is the grand total: the sum of every group's ``total``.
1261	
1262	    Instances are frozen, support positional construction and compare (and
1263	    hash) by value; no key material or randomness is involved.

1272	def merkle_verify_workload_profile(
1273	    w: Any, height: Any, groups: Any, modes: Any
1274	) -> MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile:
1275	    """Return the frozen :class:`MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile` hash counts.
1276	
1277	    Totals the SHA-256 work a verifier spends on a workload of several
1278	    independent leaf-index groups, each carried in its own batch proof or
1279	    multi-proof over the same Merkle tree. ``w`` must be 4 or 8 and
1280	    ``height`` a non-boolean integer from 1 to 8. ``groups`` must be a
1281	    non-empty tuple; each member must itself be a non-empty tuple of strictly
1282	    increasing, non-boolean integers, each in ``0 .. 2 ** height - 1`` (the
1283	    single-group rules of :func:`merkle_verify_profile`, applied per group).
1284	    ``modes`` must be a tuple of the same length as ``groups``; each entry is
1285	    ``"batch"`` or ``"multiproof"``.
1286

1288	    that profile's ``batch`` internal-node count (each signature repeats its
1289	    full authentication path) and a ``"multiproof"`` mode takes its
1290	    ``multi`` count (deduplicated merge). The per-group five-tuple is
1291	    ``(mode, wots, leaf, internal, wots + leaf + internal)`` in group order;
1292	    repeated groups are billed separately. ``total`` is the sum of every
1293	    group's three hash counts. The estimate is pure: no keys are generated,
1294	    no randomness is drawn and no state is changed.
1295	
1296	    A non-tuple ``groups`` or ``modes`` (a group that is not itself a tuple
1297	    included), or a mode entry that is not a string, raises ``TypeError``;
1298	    an empty ``groups``, a group-level mismatch with the single-group rules,
1299	    a wrong-length ``modes`` tuple or an unknown mode name raises

1302	    w = _validate_w(w)
1303	    height = _validate_height(height)
1304	    if not isinstance(groups, tuple):
1305	        raise TypeError("groups must be a tuple of leaf-index groups")
1306	    if not groups:
1307	        raise ValueError("groups must not be empty")
1308	    if not isinstance(modes, tuple):
1309	        raise TypeError("modes must be a tuple of transport mode names")
1310	    if len(modes) != len(groups):
1311	        raise ValueError("modes must have exactly one entry per group")
1312	    if any(not isinstance(mode, str) for mode in modes):
1313	        raise TypeError("every mode must be a string")
1314	    if any(mode not in ("batch", "multiproof") for mode in modes):
1315	        raise ValueError('every mode must be "batch" or "multiproof"')
1316	
1317	    costs = []
1318	    grand_total = 0
1319	    for group, mode in zip(groups, modes):
1320	        single = merkle_verify_profile(w, height, group)
1321	        internal = single.batch if mode == "batch" else single.multi
1322	        group_total = single.wots + single.leaf + internal
1323	        costs.append((mode, single.wots, single.leaf, internal, group_total))
1324	        grand_total += group_total

1326	        w=w, height=height, costs=tuple(costs), total=grand_total
1327	    )

1353	def recommend_merkle_transport_deployment(
1354	    capacity: Any,
1355	    indices: Any,
1356	    budgets: Any,
1357	    prefer: str = "multiproof",
1358	) -> MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile:
1359	    """Jointly choose Merkle tree parameters and a transport encoding.
1360	
1361	    Enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
1362	    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers both ``capacity``
1363	    and the requested leaf ``indices`` and that satisfy every set budget, and
1364	    ranks the feasible set, reusing :func:`merkle_storage_profile`,
1365	    :func:`merkle_transport_profile` and :func:`profile` for every size and
1366	    step count.
1367	
1368	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``indices``
1369	    must be a non-empty tuple of strictly increasing, non-boolean integers
1370	    whose largest member is below the candidate tree's leaf count; the same
1371	    index set is sized for every candidate. ``budgets`` must be a four-tuple,
1372	    in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
1373	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on the batch-proof wire
1374	    length (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.batch`), on the
1375	    multi-proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.multi`)
1376	    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
1377	    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
1378	    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.

1381	    first and then ``batch``, ``"batch"`` minimises ``batch`` first and then
1382	    ``multi``, and ``"speed"`` minimises steps first and then ``multi`` and

1385	    candidate after sorting is returned as a

1389	    out-of-range ``capacity``, an empty, non-integer, boolean,
1390	    out-of-range or non-strictly-increasing ``indices``, a wrong-length or
1391	    otherwise illegal ``budgets`` tuple, an unknown ``prefer`` value, or

1394	    changes no state.

1403	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
1404	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
1405	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
1406	    ):
1407	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
1408	    if not indices:
1409	        raise ValueError("indices must not be empty")
1410	    if any(isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) for index in indices):
1411	        raise ValueError("every index must be a non-boolean integer")

1424	        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:

1445	                continue

1447	                continue

1449	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:

1458	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
1459	            storage.leaf_count,
1460	            storage.w,
1461	            storage.height,

1465	        if prefer == "batch":

1478	    indices: Any,
1479	    budgets: Any,

1481	    """Return every feasible, non-dominated joint deployment as a tuple.
1482

1484	    configs and returns one, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so
1485	    a caller can inspect the trade-off between checkpoint, batch-proof,
1486	    multi-proof and verification costs: it enumerates every Merkle candidate
1487	    — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — whose leaf count
1488	    covers both ``capacity`` and the requested leaf ``indices``, keeps those
1489	    satisfying every set budget, reusing :func:`merkle_storage_profile` for
1490	    the tree wire sizes, :func:`merkle_transport_profile` for the carried
1491	    multi-proof node count and the batch/multi-proof wire sizes and
1492	    :func:`profile` for the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count, and
1493	    drops every dominated candidate.
1494	
1495	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``indices``
1496	    must be a non-empty tuple of strictly increasing, non-negative,
1497	    non-boolean integers; the same index set is sized for every candidate and
1498	    the chosen tree's leaf count must cover both ``capacity`` and the largest
1499	    index plus one. ``budgets`` must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound
1500	    on the checkpoint bytes
1501	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on the batch-proof wire
1502	    length (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.batch`), on the
1503	    multi-proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.multi`)
1504	    and on the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count
1505	    (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None``
1506	    (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at least one entry
1507	    must be set; every bound is inclusive.

1510	    ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on all four metrics — checkpoint bytes,
1511	    batch-proof wire bytes, multi-proof wire bytes and verifier steps — and
1512	    strictly smaller on at least one; every dominated candidate is dropped
1513	    and the survivors are deduplicated by value. The carried node count is
1514	    an output of :func:`merkle_transport_profile` rather than a budgeted
1515	    metric, so it never participates in dominance or ordering on its own. No
1516	    preference is applied, so a configuration trading speed for transport
1517	    size (or the reverse) is never discarded ahead of the dominance test.

1519	    multi-proof wire bytes, batch-proof wire bytes, checkpoint bytes, leaf
1520	    count, ``w`` and ``height``.

1523	    out-of-range ``capacity``, an empty, non-integer, boolean, negative or
1524	    non-strictly-increasing ``indices``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal

1527	    no keys and changes no state.

1530	        raise TypeError("indices must be a tuple of leaf indices")

1532	    if (
1533	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
1534	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
1535	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
1536	    ):
1537	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
1538	    if not indices:
1539	        raise ValueError("indices must not be empty")
1540	    if any(isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) for index in indices):
1541	        raise ValueError("every index must be a non-boolean integer")
1542	    if any(former >= latter for former, latter in zip(indices, indices[1:])):
1543	        raise ValueError("indices must be strictly increasing and unique")
1544	    if indices[0] < 0:
1545	        raise ValueError("every index must be non-negative")
1546	    checkpoint_limit, batch_limit, multi_limit, steps_limit = limits
1547	
1548	    required_leaves = max(capacity, indices[-1] + 1)
1549	    candidates: list[tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int, int, int, int]] = []
1550	    for w in (4, 8):
1551	        for height in range(1, 9):
1552	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
1553	            if storage.leaf_count < required_leaves:
1554	                continue
1555	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
1556	                continue
1557	            node_count, batch_bytes, multi_bytes = merkle_transport_profile(
1558	                w, height, indices
1559	            )
1560	            if batch_limit is not None and batch_bytes > batch_limit:
1561	                continue
1562	            if multi_limit is not None and multi_bytes > multi_limit:
1563	                continue
1564	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
1565	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
1566	                continue
1567	            candidates.append((storage, node_count, batch_bytes, multi_bytes, steps))
1568	    if not candidates:
1569	        raise ValueError(
1570	            "no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity, indices and budgets"
1571	        )
1572	
1573	    def dominates(
1574	        a: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int, int, int, int],
1575	        b: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int, int, int, int],
1576	    ) -> bool:
1577	        a_storage, _a_nodes, a_batch, a_multi, a_steps = a
1578	        b_storage, _b_nodes, b_batch, b_multi, b_steps = b
1579	        no_worse = (
1580	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes <= b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
1581	            and a_batch <= b_batch
1582	            and a_multi <= b_multi
1583	            and a_steps <= b_steps
1584	        )
1585	        strictly_better = (
1586	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes < b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
1587	            or a_batch < b_batch
1588	            or a_multi < b_multi
1589	            or a_steps < b_steps
1590	        )
1591	        return no_worse and strictly_better

1593	    non_dominated = [
1594	        candidate
1595	        for candidate in candidates
1596	        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in candidates)
1597	    ]
1598	
1599	    profiles = [
1600	        MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile(
1601	            config=storage, nodes=node_count, batch=batch_bytes, multi=multi_bytes
1602	        )
1603	        for storage, node_count, batch_bytes, multi_bytes, _steps in non_dominated
1604	    ]

"""Static parameter analysis for pqattest schemes.

:func:`profile` reports the size and cost metrics of a scheme/parameter
combination without generating any keys, and :func:`recommend` picks a Merkle
configuration for a desired signature capacity, :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment`
picks one that additionally fits deployment budgets. :func:`merkle_storage_profile`
breaks the Merkle wire sizes down per serialised object and
:func:`merkle_transport_profile` sizes a batch or multi-proof over a chosen
leaf-index set. :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment` chooses both the
tree parameters and the transport encoding together under checkpoint, batch,
multi-proof and verifier-step budgets, and
:func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier` returns every feasible,
non-dominated choice of the same joint deployment as a tuple instead of
ranking one. :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted` ranks
that same frontier by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights
over its five min-max-normalised costs — batch-proof bytes, multi-proof
bytes, carried nodes, checkpoint bytes and verifier steps — with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted_scenarios` ranks that
same joint-deployment frontier against several such weight scenarios at
once, minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload`
extends that joint choice to several independent leaf-index groups, each carried
in its own transport, under checkpoint, per-group, aggregate and verifier-step
budgets. :func:`merkle_transport_workload_frontier` returns every feasible,
non-dominated choice of the same workload as a tuple instead of ranking one.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted` ranks that same
frontier by a caller-supplied four-tuple of non-negative weights over its
four min-max-normalised costs in the order checkpoint bytes, single-group
peak, aggregate transport and verifier steps (the weighted sum divided by
the weight total), with exact :class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and
returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted_scenarios` ranks that
same workload frontier against several such weight scenarios at once,
minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`merkle_mode_frontier` goes further and enumerates every per-group
``batch``/``multiproof`` mode combination of the workload under checkpoint,
per-group, aggregate, verifier-step and carried-node budgets, returning the
feasible, non-dominated mode choices as a tuple.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_deployment` ranks that mode frontier by a
business preference — ``"compact"``, ``"nodes"`` or ``"speed"`` — and
returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted` instead ranks that same mode frontier
by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights over its five
min-max-normalised costs in the order checkpoint bytes, single-group peak,
aggregate transport, verifier steps and carried nodes (the weighted sum
divided by the weight total), with exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios` instead ranks that same
mode frontier against several five-tuples of non-negative cost weights at
once — checkpoint bytes, single-group peak, aggregate transport, verifier
steps and carried nodes — minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then
regret sum, then per-scenario scores) with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`merkle_deployment_frontier` likewise returns the whole Pareto frontier
of ordinary Merkle deployments under checkpoint, signature, proof and
verifier-step budgets. :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted` ranks
that same ordinary-deployment frontier by a caller-supplied four-tuple of
non-negative weights over its four min-max-normalised costs in the order
checkpoint bytes, signature wire length, standalone proof wire length and
verifier steps (the weighted sum divided by the weight total), with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted_scenarios` ranks that same
ordinary-deployment frontier against several such four-weight scenarios
at once — checkpoint bytes, signature wire length, standalone proof wire
length and verifier steps — minimising the worst per-scenario regret
(then regret sum, then per-scenario scores) with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`explain_merkle_deployment_weighted` exports the decision-cost
breakdown behind that same weighted ranking as a tuple of frozen
:class:`MerkleDeploymentScore` rows — one per frontier member, in
frontier order, each carrying the candidate's config, its four
normalised costs, its final score and a selected flag — with the same
exact :class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic.
:func:`merkle_verify_profile` compares the
verifier-side SHA-256 hash cost of a batch proof against a multi-proof over
the same leaf set, returning a :class:`MerkleVerifyProfile`.
:func:`merkle_verify_workload_profile` extends that comparison to several
independent leaf-index groups, each carried in its own ``"batch"`` or
``"multiproof"`` transport, and totals the per-group SHA-256 work in a
:class:`MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile`. :func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier`
joins the two: it enumerates every per-group mode combination of every
candidate config under checkpoint, per-group peak, aggregate transport,
verifier-step, carried-node and verifier-hash budgets, returning the
feasible, non-dominated choices as frozen :class:`MerkleModeCost` tuples.
:func:`merkle_cardinality_frontier` is the worst-case-position counterpart
for workloads where only each group's leaf count is fixed: every
multi-proof group is billed at the maximum transport bytes, canonical node
count and internal-node hash count over every same-size strictly
increasing index subset of the candidate tree, and it returns the same
feasible, non-dominated :class:`MerkleModeCost` frontier.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_deployment` ranks that cardinality
frontier by one of five preferences — ``"compact"``, ``"verify"``,
``"nodes"``, ``"speed"`` or ``"robust"`` — and returns one
:class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted` ranks the same frontier by a
caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights over its five
min-max-normalised costs, all arithmetic exact via :class:`fractions.Fraction`,
and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`explain_merkle_cardinality_weighted` exports the decision-cost
breakdown behind that same weighted cardinality ranking as a tuple of frozen
:class:`MerkleCardinalityScore` rows — one per frontier member, in frontier
order, each carrying the candidate's plan/cost pairing, its five normalised
costs, its final score and a selected flag — with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_weighted` ranks the fixed-position
:func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier` frontier against several weight scenarios
at once, minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted_scenarios` applies that same
preference-drift-robust multi-scenario minimax-regret ranking to the
worst-case-position :func:`merkle_cardinality_frontier` frontier.
:func:`explain_merkle_cardinality_weighted_scenarios` exports the
decision-cost breakdown behind that same multi-scenario cardinality
ranking as a tuple of frozen :class:`MerkleCardinalityScenarioScore`
rows — one per frontier member, in frontier order, each carrying the
candidate's plan/cost pairing, its five normalised costs, its
per-scenario scores and regrets and a selected flag — with the same
exact :class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment` ranks the fixed-position
:func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier` frontier by one of five business
preferences — ``"compact"``, ``"verify"``, ``"nodes"``, ``"speed"`` or
``"robust"`` — and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment_weighted` ranks that same
fixed-position frontier by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative
weights over its five min-max-normalised costs (total transport,
single-group peak, total verifier hashes, carried nodes and per-signature
chain steps), the weighted sum divided by the weight total with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one
:class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_scheme` is the cross-scheme selector: it enumerates every
configuration :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes and both
Merkle ``w`` choices at every tree height — keeps those covering the
requested signature count and fitting a two-tuple of signature-size and
chain-step budgets, and ranks the feasible set by a ``"size"`` or
``"speed"`` preference, returning one :class:`Params`.
All thirty-four
are pure functions: no randomness, no
state, no I/O, no keys are generated.
"""

_SCHEMES = ("lamport", "wots", "merkle")
_MAX_CAPACITY = 256


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    """Frozen metrics for one scheme/parameter combination.

    ``capacity`` is the number of messages one key pair can sign; ``elements``
    the number of 32-byte chain elements per (one-time) signature;
    ``sig_bytes`` and ``path_bytes`` the serialised signature and
    authentication-path sizes in bytes, excluding any leaf index and Python
    object overhead; ``steps`` the upper bound on hash-chain steps a verifier
    performs per (one-time) signature. ``w``/``height`` are ``None`` when the
    scheme does not use them.
    """

    scheme: str
    w: int | None
    height: int | None
    capacity: int
    elements: int
    sig_bytes: int
    path_bytes: int
    steps: int


def _wots_metrics(w: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return ``(n, steps)``: chain count and chain-step upper bound."""
    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    n = l1 + l2
    return n, n * (b - 1)


def profile(scheme: str, w: Any = None, height: Any = None) -> Params:
    """Return the :class:`Params` metrics for a scheme configuration.

    ``lamport`` takes neither ``w`` nor ``height``; ``wots`` takes ``w`` (4 or
    8) only; ``merkle`` takes both (``height`` an integer from 1 to 8). An
    unknown scheme, a missing parameter or an unexpected one raises
    ``ValueError``.
    """
    if scheme == "lamport":
        if w is not None or height is not None:
            raise ValueError("lamport takes neither w nor height")
        return Params(
            scheme="lamport",
            w=None,
            height=None,
            capacity=1,
            elements=0,
            sig_bytes=256 * 32,
            path_bytes=0,
            steps=0,
        )
    if scheme == "wots":
        if w is None:
            raise ValueError("wots requires w")
        if height is not None:
            raise ValueError("wots takes no height")
        w = _validate_w(w)
        n, steps = _wots_metrics(w)
        return Params(
            scheme="wots",
            w=w,
            height=None,
            capacity=1,
            elements=n,
            sig_bytes=n * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            path_bytes=0,
            steps=steps,
        )
    if scheme == "merkle":
        if w is None or height is None:
            raise ValueError("merkle requires both w and height")
        w = _validate_w(w)
        height = _validate_height(height)
        n, steps = _wots_metrics(w)
        return Params(
            scheme="merkle",
            w=w,
            height=height,
            capacity=1 << height,
            elements=n,
            sig_bytes=(n + height) * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            path_bytes=height * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            steps=steps,
        )
    raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}")


def recommend(capacity: Any, prefer: str = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the Merkle :class:`Params` covering ``capacity`` signatures.

    ``capacity`` must be an integer from 1 to 256 (non-bool); the height is
    the smallest one with ``2 ** height >= capacity`` and at least 1.
    ``prefer="size"`` picks ``w=8`` (shorter signatures), ``prefer="speed"``
    picks ``w=4`` (fewer chain steps). Anything else raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer == "size":
        w = 8
    elif prefer == "speed":
        w = 4
    else:
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
    height = max(1, (capacity - 1).bit_length())
    return profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)


def recommend_scheme(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the :class:`Params` of the scheme best fitting capacity/budgets.

    The cross-scheme counterpart of :func:`recommend`: instead of choosing
    only among Merkle configurations, enumerate every configuration
    :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS
    with ``w`` 4 and 8) and every Merkle configuration with ``w`` in
    ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — keep those whose ``capacity``
    covers the requested signature count and that satisfy both budgets, and
    rank the feasible set. The one-time candidates cover one signature and
    are present only when ``capacity == 1``; a request for more than one
    signature leaves the Merkle configurations as the only candidates.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
    signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and on the
    verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`). Each entry is
    either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at
    least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` (the default) ranks candidates by ``sig_bytes`` first
    and ``steps`` second; ``prefer="speed"`` reverses the two. Both share
    the same ascending tie-break afterwards: spare capacity
    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), the scheme
    name lexicographically, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing
    parameter sorted ahead of any value. The first candidate after sorting
    is returned as a :class:`Params`.

    Validation runs capacity first, budgets second and ``prefer`` last. A
    non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a boolean, non-integer or
    out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal
    ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``), an unknown
    ``prefer`` value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises
    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
    no keys and changes no state.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 2-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 2:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly two entries")

    labels = ("signature", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
    signature_limit, steps_limit = limits

    candidates: list[Params] = []
    if capacity == 1:
        candidates.append(profile("lamport"))
        for w in (4, 8):
            candidates.append(profile("wots", w=w))
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            candidate = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)
            if candidate.capacity >= capacity:
                candidates.append(candidate)

    feasible = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
            continue
        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
            continue
        feasible.append(candidate)
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
        tail = (
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (candidate.steps, candidate.sig_bytes) + tail
        return (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) + tail

    return min(feasible, key=ranking)


def recommend_merkle_deployment(
    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.

    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)
    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` ranks candidates lexicographically by signature wire
    length, proof wire length, checkpoint bytes, steps, leaf count, ``w`` and
    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.

    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
    no state.
    """
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')

    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits

    feasible = []
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
                continue
            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
                continue
            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
                continue
            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
                continue
            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
                continue
            feasible.append((storage, steps))
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        storage, steps = candidate
        ordered = (
            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
            steps,
            storage.leaf_count,
            storage.w,
            storage.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (steps,) + ordered
        return ordered

    feasible.sort(key=ranking)
    return feasible[0][0]


def _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets: Any) -> tuple[int | None, ...]:
    """Validate the four-tuple of deployment budget limits."""
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    return tuple(limits)

    """Validate the four-tuple of checkpoint/batch/multi-proof/steps limits."""

    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    labels = ("checkpoint", "batch", "multiproof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:

        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:

    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
